answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because karst only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, ivory is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any anchor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
